The biggest sins are joining others with Allah, undutifulness to parents, and false witness or the Ghamus oath, a false oath taking a Muslim's property.
Whoever does good in Islam is not punished for pre-Islamic deeds, but whoever does evil in Islam is punished for both his former and later deeds.
Ibn Abbas cited the Prophet's order to kill, not burn, whoever changes his religion; Mu'adh insisted a man reverting to Judaism be killed; Abu Bakr resolved to fight Zakat refusers.
When Jews greeted the Prophet with 'death be upon you', he forbade killing the one who said it, told Aisha to be gentle, and taught replying 'and upon you'.
The Prophet told of one of the prophets who, beaten and bloodied by his people, wiped his face and asked his Lord to forgive them, for they did not know.
The Prophet foretold people whose Quran recital never passes their throats, who leave the religion like an arrow through game, and said to kill them; Ali killed them.
The Hour will not come until two great groups fight each other while making one and the same claim.
Umar dragged Hisham to the Prophet for reciting Surat al-Furqan differently; the Prophet approved both readings, saying the Quran was revealed to be recited in seven ways.
When the companions feared the verse on not mixing belief with wrong, the Prophet said the wrong meant joining others in worship with Allah, as Luqman told his son.
When a man called Malik bin Ad-Dukhshun a hypocrite, the Prophet said whoever meets Allah saying none is worshipped but Allah, for Allah's sake, will be saved from the Fire.
Ali seized Hatib's letter to the Meccans from a woman; Umar wanted him killed as a betrayer, but the Prophet accepted his excuse and spared him as one of Badr.
In his prayer the Prophet asked Allah to save Aiyash, Salama, Al-Walid and the weak believers, and to afflict Mudar with famine years like Joseph's.
Faith's sweetness belongs to whoever holds Allah and His Messenger dearest, loves others only for Allah, and hates returning to disbelief as he hates being thrown into the Fire.
Sa'id bin Zaid recalled Umar binding him to force him from Islam, and the Prophet told complaining companions that earlier believers sawn in two never left their religion.
At Bait al-Midras the Prophet thrice called the Jews to embrace Islam and be safe, then said he wanted to exile them, so those with property could sell it.
The Prophet annulled the marriage of Khansa, given by her father against her wish, and said a woman's consent is required, a shy virgin's silence counting as consent.
When an Ansari made his only property, a slave, free upon his death, the Prophet sold the slave to Nu'aim bin An-Nahham for 800 dirhams.
The verse forbidding inheriting women against their will concerns a pre-Islamic custom whereby a dead man's relatives could marry his wife, marry her off or stop her marrying.
Umar flogged and exiled a male slave who forced himself on a slave girl, not flogging her as she was unwilling; Az-Zuhri added a fine for raping a virgin slave.
When a tyrant demanded Sarah from Abraham and sought to harm her, she made ablution and prayed, and the king was seized by a fit.
A Muslim neither wrongs his brother nor hands him to an oppressor, Allah meets the needs of one meeting his brother's, and an oppressor brother is helped by being stopped.
Deeds are rewarded by intentions, so one emigrating for Allah and His Messenger has that, and one emigrating for worldly gain or a woman has what he sought.
Allah does not accept the prayer of one who has passed wind until he performs ablution anew.
Abu Bakr's letter forbade merging or splitting property to avoid Zakat, treasure whose Zakat is unpaid becomes a snake on Resurrection Day, and some people allowed tricks to escape it.
The Prophet forbade Shighar, exchanging daughters or sisters in marriage without Mahr, and Mut'a marriage at Khaibar, while some people judged such marriages made by trick valid or invalid.
No one should withhold his surplus water from others' animals in order to keep them from the surplus grass.
The Prophet forbade An-Najsh and told a man who was always cheated in bargains to say 'No cheating' whenever he bargained.
Aisha explained the verse on orphan girls: guardians drawn by their wealth and beauty were forbidden to marry them with less than a full Mahr.
Every betrayer will have a flag by which he is recognised on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet, only human, judges by what he hears, so whoever is wrongly awarded his brother's right by an eloquent case is given only a piece of Fire.
A virgin or matron is married only with her consent, a virgin's silence counting, and Khansa's forced marriage was cancelled, though some people upheld marriages faked through false witnesses.
When the Prophet stayed long with Hafsa drinking honey, Aisha had Sauda and Safiya say he smelled of Maghafir, a trick that made him refuse the honey thereafter.
Umar turned back from Sargh on hearing the Prophet's saying, from Abdur-Rahman, not to enter a plague-stricken land nor flee one, plague being a punishment sent on nations.
One who takes back his gift is like a dog swallowing its own vomit, an example believers should not follow.
The Prophet gave pre-emption in undivided property and said a neighbour has most right to his neighbour's care, yet some people allowed tricks like gifts or share-buying to defeat it.
The Prophet rebuked a Zakat collector claiming gifts, asking whether he would get them at his parents' home, and warned that anything taken unlawfully is carried on Resurrection Day.
The neighbour has most right to his neighbour's care, yet some allowed a sham price trick to defeat pre-emption, though the Prophet forbade selling Muslims defective or stolen goods.

Revelation began with true dreams and the angel's command to read in Hira; Khadija comforted the Prophet, Waraqa recognised the angel, and when revelation paused Gabriel reassured him on mountaintops.
A good dream is from Allah, one of forty-six parts of prophethood and its only remnant; a bad dream is from Satan, harmless if one seeks refuge and spits left.
Some were shown the Night of Qadr in the last seven days of Ramadan, and the Prophet said to seek it then.
